content.text: Section 22 matches the preferred position on all parameters, and Section 23 (Records) contains only a heading with no substantive access rights, so there is no broader inspection right binding us.

input.quote: 22.2 Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.
input.rationale: Section 22 meets the preferred position in full: audits of Customer are limited to once in any twelve-month period (22.1), require at least thirty days' prior written notice and normal business hours (22.1), must be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (22.1), are at Vendor's cost unless an underpayment exceeding five percent is established (22.2), and expressly bar direct access to Customer systems, unrelated Customer Data, privileged material and third-party confidential information (22.2). Section 22.3 further confines use of findings to enforcement and treats them as Customer Confidential Information. No broader inspection or verification right binding Customer exists elsewhere — Section 23 (Records and Customer Assurance) contains only a heading with no operative text, and no monitoring, telemetry, premises-inspection or remote-access rights against Customer appear in the document. No redline required.
